samples.summary: Label recomputation is O(lines × spans) per document change, over a span list that grows with every keystroke
samples.evidence: `authorOfRange` restarts `for (const span of spans)` from index 0 for every line (`if (span.to <= from) continue;` only skips, it does not advance a cursor), and `computeBlameLabels` calls it once per line, so each doc change costs lines × spans iterations. The span list is not bounded by note length: `YorkieNoteStore.editText` stamps a distinct `t: Date.now()` on every insert, so adjacent runs never share attributes and `Text.values()` yields roughly one run per edit. `NoteBlameTracker.update` (line 136) re-runs the whole walk on every `docChanged` update, i.e. on every keystroke while the gutter is on. On a long, heavily edited note (e.g. 1k lines × several thousand runs) this is millions of iterations plus a fresh span array allocation per keystroke — typing lag that gets monotonically worse as the note is edited.

samples.summary: Attribution attributes are written on every insert regardless of whether the gutter is enabled, so all notes pay unbounded CRDT run growth
samples.evidence: `editText` always takes the `insert.length > 0` branch and writes `{a: name, t: Date.now()}`; nothing consults `showAuthors`. Because `t` differs per millisecond, every keystroke produces a new, unmergeable run in `root.content`, so run count (and hence snapshot/wire size) grows with edit count for every user of every note — including the ones who never turn the feature on. This also contradicts the stated invariant in this change: `notes-view.tsx:31` ("renders exactly as before the gutter existed") and `docs/design/notes/notes.md:517` ("a reader who never turns it on gets ... none of the per-edit bookkeeping") are false as written, since the bookkeeping is unconditional in the store.

samples.summary: MemNoteStore.splice spreads one argument per inserted character, which throws RangeError on a large paste
samples.evidence: `this.authors.splice(from, to - from, ...new Array<MemAuthorMark>(insert.length).fill(mark))` passes `insert.length` arguments to `splice`. Engines cap argument count (~65k–125k in V8), so a single paste/programmatic insert of a large markdown file into a MemNoteStore-backed editor throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` from inside `editText`, aborting the edit after `this.text` was already updated on line 126 — leaving `text` and `authors` different lengths (a broken invariant) even if the throw is caught upstream.

samples.summary: Collapsing consecutive same-author lines can leave the entire visible gutter blank when scrolled
samples.evidence: `labels.push(author !== null && author !== previous ? author : '')` computes collapse over the whole document, but CodeMirror only renders gutter markers for viewport lines. Scrolling into the middle of a long run written by one author shows no label at all on any visible line, because the only labelled line of the run is off-screen above — the gutter conveys nothing exactly where a reader would look. No viewport-aware re-anchoring exists (`lineMarker` just indexes the precomputed array at line 207).

samples.summary: "Most recent edit wins" is decided by unsynchronized client wall clocks
samples.evidence: `t: Date.now()` is each client's local clock, and `authorOfRange` (blame-gutter.ts:48) picks the span with the largest `at`. A peer whose clock runs fast permanently outranks everyone on any line it ever touched, and a peer whose clock is behind can edit a line and never appear as its author — the label is then simply wrong rather than merely imprecise. Yorkie's own lamport/actor ordering is available and is not used for the tiebreak.

finding.summary: Label recomputation is O(lines × spans) per document change, over a span list that grows with every keystroke
finding.evidence: `authorOfRange` restarts `for (const span of spans)` from index 0 for every line (`if (span.to <= from) continue;` only skips, it does not advance a cursor), and `computeBlameLabels` calls it once per line, so each doc change costs lines × spans iterations. The span list is not bounded by note length: `YorkieNoteStore.editText` stamps a distinct `t: Date.now()` on every insert, so adjacent runs never share attributes and `Text.values()` yields roughly one run per edit. `NoteBlameTracker.update` (line 136) re-runs the whole walk on every `docChanged` update, i.e. on every keystroke while the gutter is on. On a long, heavily edited note (e.g. 1k lines × several thousand runs) this is millions of iterations plus a fresh span array allocation per keystroke — typing lag that gets monotonically worse as the note is edited.

verdict.reason: The described code exists: authorOfRange (blame-gutter.ts:37-52) rescans the span prefix from index 0 for each line (it does break at span.from >= to, line 45), computeBlameLabels calls it per line (65-74), and NoteBlameTracker.update recomputes on every docChanged (136-145) over a freshly allocated span array (yorkie-note-store.ts:101-126) whose runs never merge because editText stamps a distinct Date.now() (yorkie-note-store.ts:90-94). So the ~O(lines x spans) per-keystroke cost is factually there. However, this is a performance/algorithmic-complexity concern, not a correctness defect: the labels produced are correct, there is no wrong condition, boundary error, missing guard, dropped await, state corruption, or leak (sameLabels at 78-81 also suppresses redundant repaint dispatches, so no transaction loop). It therefore falls outside the Correctness lane, whose major bar is "a real logic bug or clearly wrong behavior". Two facts also cut the claimed magnitude: the span list IS bounded by note length (getAuthorSpans skips zero-length runs at yorkie-note-store.ts:108, so spans.length <= doc.length, and deletions remove runs), contradicting the "not bounded by note length / monotonically worse" premise; and the whole feature is opt-in and off by default (editor.ts:271, with the gutter/tracker compartments installing [] at editor.ts:356 and 388), so the walk does not exist for users who never enable it. Real, but belongs to a performance lens rather than blocking on correctness.

verdict.reason: The code is present as described — `editText` unconditionally writes `{a, t}` on any non-empty insert and never consults `showAuthors` (yorkie-note-store.ts:84-99) — but it is not a correctness defect. (1) It is the explicit, documented design: notes.md:520-524 specifies attributes written by `YorkieNoteStore.editText`, and notes.md:545-550 budgets the cost ("~30 bytes of attribute JSON per inserted run... a constant factor on existing per-run overhead... Retention... deliberately unbounded for now"). Storage/wire growth accepted by design is a design/performance judgment, not logic or runtime correctness: no wrong condition, no crash, no data loss, no leaked resource. (2) The proposed gating would be incorrect: `showAuthors` is a per-viewer, localStorage-persisted rendering preference (notes-settings.ts:11, notes-view.tsx:154-156, editor.ts:517-527 reconfigures only local compartments), so skipping shared-CRDT attribution when the local user's gutter is off would blank out attribution for collaborators who do enable it. (3) The cited invariants are misread: notes-view.tsx:29-33 says a mount without the prop "renders exactly as before" — a rendering claim that holds (editor.ts:356,388 contribute no extension when off). Only "none of the per-edit bookkeeping" (notes.md:516-518) is loose prose, immediately qualified by the Storage bullet — a doc wording nit, not blocking. Attribution-on-write is the store contract generally: MemNoteStore records it on every insert too (memory.ts:80-98).
